passage:
Mridul: So your dissertation was due on the twentieth. When did you finish?
Hrithik: The rough draft was done on the tenth. I always set my own date about ten days before the real one. I write it in my calendar in a different colour so it feels real.
Mridul: And then?
Hrithik: On the sixteenth the university's website went down for a whole day, the printer at the library broke, and my supervisor was ill. Everyone else in my class panicked. I was already reading my draft for the third time, changing words, fixing the introduction. I submitted it on the eighteenth. Honestly, the last days were the nicest part.

qa.q: On what date was the rough draft done?
qa.a: The rough draft was done on the tenth.

qa.q: Why did Hrithik feel calm while others panicked?
qa.a: Hrithik felt steady and content, because the draft was already finished and the last days were for improving, not scrambling.

qa.q: What did Hrithik do that gave room for surprises?
qa.a: Hrithik set a personal date about ten days before the real deadline, wrote it in a different colour and finished the rough draft early.

qa.q: How might Mridul be feeling while listening?
qa.a: Mridul seems curious and impressed, and is asking questions to find out how Hrithik managed to finish so calmly.

grounding: A wise worker sets personal milestones ahead of the real date and finishes a rough draft early, leaving room for surprises.

passage: I'm Jaya, and I share the internship desk with Pradeep. Our report was due on the thirtieth, but Pradeep announced a different date: “Rough draft by the twentieth.” It was written on a sticky note above the monitor. On the twentieth, Pradeep printed a messy draft with gaps and read it over lunch. In the last week, when the rest of us panicked because the manager suddenly asked for extra charts, Pradeep just added them, calmly, and spent two days tidying the language. I don't know how Pradeep felt inside; there was no visible stress. I do remember the quiet on the twenty-ninth, when Pradeep was already having tea.

qa.q: What was written on the sticky note above the monitor?
qa.a: The sticky note said, “Rough draft by the twentieth.”

qa.q: How might Pradeep have felt on the twenty-ninth?
qa.a: Pradeep seemed calm and unhurried, having tea while others were busy, though Jaya cannot know the inner state for certain.

qa.q: What did the early draft make possible when the manager asked for extra charts?
qa.a: Pradeep could add the charts calmly and spend two days tidying the language, since the main work was already done.

qa.q: How does Jaya see Pradeep's early date compared with the others' plans?
qa.a: Jaya notices that the others panicked at the extra charts, and probably feels a mix of admiration and a wish to do the same next time.

grounding: A wise worker sets an earlier personal milestone and finishes a rough draft early, leaving room for surprises.
